There has been major problems with Spectrum/Charter/TWC/Roadrunner lately. Neither mail.twc.com (TWC's email servers) or mobile.charter.net (Spectrum and Charter's servers) appear to be online right now and may have been down for some time. From what we hear from their users, service has been intermittent for a while but it's gotten worse in the past week or few. It is not specifically a Thunderbird issue - it appears to affect most or all 3rd-party email clients, including Outlook, eMClient, etc. Spectrum's support usually (but not always!) won't admit to any problems, only saying that they only support webmail.

Here's a link to Spectrum's own user forum where you can see many discussions of the situation:

https://community.spectrum.net/categories/email-22

If you have time and patience you could contact Spectrum for status.

I have seen mention of a possible temporary workaround, which is to change the SMTP server to "mail.brighthouse.com". I can't verify that this works, or if it does that it won't quit working at any time, but it's easy enough to try and you can change it back to the existing name if it's not effective.

Otherwise, until they fix their servers your only recourse for now is to use their webmail. Or find another, more reliable email provider.

content:
Please describe what you mean by "move my Microsoft 365 account". Do you mean you're closing it and moving to another email provider?

Local folders are independent of any email accounts you have set up in Thunderbird. They will persist no matter what other email accounts you add or remove. If you copy all folders and messages from the Microsoft account to Thunderbird's Local Folders they will not be affected by removing that Microsoft account.

Before making any major changes to accounts in Thunderbird, it's good practice to make a backup of your Profile so you can recover if something unexpected happens. Actually, you should make regular backups of the Profile if you email is valuable to you.

Export your Thunderbird Profile https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-export

content:
I have a feeling the issue is with the mail server here.

What mail provider offers the mail account in question? Or is it perhaps self hosted?

Normally an IMAP server lists the folder to be used as deleted/trash/deleted item with a flag that Thunderbird recognizes.

SO there are I think a couple of possible points of failure. 1. Thunderbird is struggling with the server namespace in the IMAP context. 2. The server folder is not being correctly identified when Thunderbird connects.

Both of these things tend to appear more on self hosted servers, but they are both under normal IMAP standards, so with the server we might be able to work out a more concrete cause.

My other issue is what happen if you select Thunderbird to not load with the operating system? I have a feeling it might be a race condition exposed by the hurly burly of startup and a thousand an one things being done at once.

When you enabled POP on gmail when did you enable it from? The default is I think the day you enable it. which would mean you will have to wait for new mail to get anything locally.

Go to this link and check your settings, https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#settings/fwdandpop

Now we need to discuss folders, and there complete absence from the POP protocol. The protocol talks of a "mail drop" and for practical reasons this is generally considered to be the inbox. This not a bad analogy, but the mail drop is all incoming mail, including what the provider considers SPAM.

Now in Thunderbird removing an account usually does not remove folder or data, unless you explicitly request that with the account removal. Nor does adding the same email address again result in anything being copied. YOu will have profile/imap Mail folder with your gmail IMAP data still in it probably. And a new folder in Profile/POP with your new account. The MSF file is created automatically as soon as you select to view the folder. It is not some hangover from the past.

Thunderbird is only really meant to work with google oauth authentication. however I would suggest you delete the existing oAUth tokens in your passwords in Thunderbird for Google so the process can start again. Google and Thunderbird might struggle with the change from IMAP to POP https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/password-manager-remember-delete-change-tb
